title: Sleep Calculation Methodology
overview: Sleep calculators estimate optimal bedtime or wake time based on sleep cycles. Each sleep cycle lasts approximately 90 minutes, and waking between cycles (rather than during deep sleep) generally leads to feeling more refreshed.

methods.name: 90-Minute Sleep Cycle Method
methods.description: Sleep occurs in cycles of approximately 90 minutes (75-120 minutes). Each cycle progresses through light sleep, deep sleep, and REM sleep.

formula.name: Sleep Cycle Calculation
formula.expression:
Optimal bedtimes = Wake Time - (n × 90 min) - 15 min
Where n = 4, 5, or 6 cycles

limitations: Time to fall asleep varies significantly
First cycles have more deep sleep, later have more REM

methods.name: NSF Sleep Duration Guidelines
methods.description: National Sleep Foundation evidence-based recommendations for total sleep duration by age group.

formula.name: NSF Recommendations (2015)
formula.expression:
Adults 18-64: 7-9 hours
Older Adults 65+: 7-8 hours
Teenagers 14-17: 8-10 hours
School age 6-13: 9-11 hours
formula.description: Optimal range for most individuals in each age group

limitations: Quality matters as much as quantity

methods.name: Chronotype Consideration
methods.description: Individual circadian rhythm preferences (morningness-eveningness) affect optimal sleep timing. 'Night owls' and 'early birds' have different ideal sleep windows.

formula.name: Chronotype Adjustment
formula.expression:
Early chronotype: Bedtime 9-10 PM, Wake 5-6 AM
Intermediate: Bedtime 10-11 PM, Wake 6-7 AM
Late chronotype: Bedtime 11 PM-12 AM, Wake 7-8 AM

limitations: Social and work schedules may not align

sources.name: National Sleep Foundation Sleep Duration Recommendations
Ohayon et al. - Sleep Duration Guidelines Systematic Review

footnotes: Sleep efficiency (time asleep vs time in bed) typically 85-95%
Alcohol, caffeine, and blue light affect sleep quality
Consistent sleep schedule is as important as duration
Deep sleep decreases with age; this is normal
disclaimer: Sleep recommendations are general guidelines. Persistent sleep problems, excessive sleepiness, or sleep disorders should be evaluated by a healthcare provider or sleep specialist.
